description: We are a team that strives for victory and educational growth—both for ourselves and for the other participants. Our primary objective is to succeed in this activity and to be the best. Key skills that we possess and cultivate include a strong grasp of the subject matter, the ability to develop it further, and a commitment to conscious, deliberate effort.
summary: We developed an interactive web experience that tells the story of Ingenuity—the NASA helicopter that flew on Mars—from its own perspective. It includes a flight log and a laboratory that compares gravity on Earth and Mars. Addressing the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge, the project transforms dense NASA technical reports into a narrative and a simulator designed for students aged 8 to 14, using exclusively official data. This is significant because, while young people are often familiar with active rovers, they are frequently unaware of the machines that have already completed their missions. The experience works offline and is free of charge, making it accessible to any educational center.
details: Our project centers on a simulation of the operations of "Ginny" (the robotic helicopter that flew on Mars), providing an engaging educational tool for students aged 8 to 14. The intended impact of *Ginny's Flight Log* is to democratize space education and preserve scientific history among young people in this age group. We developed the project using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. It is designed as an educational and informative resource, grounded in historical research conducted using official NASA sources.
